title: Police Officer Written Exam — NBPD style
source: Entry-level police written exam practice in the shape used by California agencies: arithmetic and word problems, reading comprehension with inference, grammar and report clarity, logic, table reading, observation recall, vocabulary and situational judgment. NBPD publishes no exam blueprint; this deck mirrors the standard section mix, not leaked items.

questions.stem: An officer works 11.25 hours per shift. Hours in 16 shifts?
questions.why: Eleven and a quarter hours across sixteen shifts comes to one hundred eighty hours.

questions.stem: A report is 40% complete after 6 pages. Total pages?
questions.why: Six pages is forty percent of the total, so the report runs fifteen pages.

questions.stem: Calls rise from 1,240 to 1,488. Percent increase?
questions.why: The increase of 248 divided by the base of 1,240 equals twenty percent.

questions.stem: A vehicle travels 42 miles in 35 minutes. Average speed?
questions.why: Forty-two miles in thirty-five minutes works out to seventy-two miles per hour.

questions.stem: Overtime is 1.5x a $41.20 hourly rate. Overtime rate?
questions.why: Forty-one dollars twenty cents times one and a half is sixty-one eighty.

questions.stem: Four districts report 320, 410, 275 and 515 calls. Mean?
questions.why: The four district figures total 1,520, which divided by four is 380.

questions.stem: The staffing model assumes six percent attrition, a figure the chief calls optimistic. He expects attrition to:
questions.why: Calling the estimate optimistic means he expects a worse number.

questions.stem: A policy applies 'notwithstanding prior practice.' The policy:
questions.why: 'Notwithstanding' displaces what came before.

questions.stem: A memo says the response 'was not inconsistent with policy.' This means the response:
questions.why: Double negative: it does not contradict policy.

questions.stem: A witness statement that is 'material' to a case is one that:
questions.why: Material means relevant to the result.

questions.stem: A sergeant writes that a trend 'bears watching.' She is recommending:
questions.why: Bears watching means keep observing.

questions.stem: 'The unit operated at reduced capacity for cause.' The reduction was:
questions.why: For cause means it had a stated justification.

questions.stem: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Neither the officer nor the sergeant was available.
Neither the officer or the sergeant were available.
Neither the officer nor the sergeant were available.
Neither the officer or the sergeant was available.
questions.why: Neither/nor takes the singular verb with a singular second subject.

questions.stem: Choose the clearest report line.
options: The vehicle was observed by me proceeding at speed.
I observed the vehicle speeding in the northbound lanes.
A high rate of speed was being proceeded at.
Speeding was observed on the part of the vehicle.
questions.why: Active voice, shortest construction, no nominalisation.

questions.stem: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
options: The suspect fled and, the officer pursued.
The suspect fled; and the officer pursued.
The suspect fled, and the officer pursued.
The suspect fled and the officer, pursued.
questions.why: Two independent clauses joined by a comma and conjunction.

questions.stem: Choose the sentence with the correct possessive.
questions.why: Singular possessive takes apostrophe before s.

questions.stem: Choose the most precise sentence.
options: The vehicle stopped at the marked crosswalk.
The vehicle stopped at the object there.
The vehicle halted near the crossing area.
The vehicle stopped in that general area.
questions.why: Concrete nouns and one verb beat vague phrasing.

questions.stem: All patrol officers are POST-certified. Some POST-certified staff are dispatchers. Therefore:
options: no dispatcher is a patrol officer
questions.why: The overlap between the two groups is undetermined.

questions.stem: If the alert is issued, the road closes. The road is not closed. Therefore:
questions.why: Denying the consequent is valid here.

questions.stem: Every report reviewed was signed. One report was unsigned. Therefore that report:
questions.why: Contrapositive of the first statement.

questions.stem: Four units respond in order: A before B, C after B, D before A. Which unit is first?
questions.why: D before A before B before C.

questions.stem: Calls by district are 320, 410, 275 and 515. Range?
questions.why: The highest district figure is 515 and the lowest is 275, a range of 240.

questions.stem: A table shows 60 stops in January and 75 in February. Percent change?
questions.why: Fifteen additional stops over a base of sixty is a twenty-five percent rise.

questions.stem: A chart shows arrests falling for three straight quarters, then rising. The trend is:
questions.why: The trend changed direction from falling to rising, which is a reversal.

questions.stem: Address given was 1450 Birch Street at 2247 hours. What was the address?
questions.why: Detail recall: number and street name.

questions.stem: The caller in that report was a 61-year-old female. The caller was:
questions.why: Age and sex were both stated.

questions.stem: The report noted a broken rear window. Which window was broken?
questions.why: Detail recall from the short passage.

questions.stem: 'The officer's account was corroborated by video.' Corroborated means:
questions.why: Corroborate means to support with evidence.

questions.stem: 'A prudent course of action' most nearly means:
questions.why: Prudent means showing care for consequences.

questions.stem: 'The order was rescinded' means the order was:
questions.why: Rescind means to revoke.

questions.stem: Two roommates argue loudly, no weapons visible. Your first action?
options: interview both roommates together at once
issue a citation to the louder roommate
separate parties and secure the scene
leave after documenting the call details
questions.why: Safety and separation before resolution.

questions.stem: A supervisor's order conflicts with written policy. You should:
options: refuse the order in front of others
follow it silently and say nothing more
report the supervisor before you comply
raise the conflict and ask clarification
questions.why: Raise it on the record, do not refuse in the field.

questions.stem: A bystander films you during a stop and refuses to stop filming. You should:
options: continue the stop and document the filming
seize the phone as evidence of interference
end the stop to avoid being recorded
order the bystander to delete the footage
questions.why: Recording is lawful; the stop continues.

questions.stem: A briefing begins at 0645 and runs 95 minutes. End time?
questions.why: Ninety-five minutes after 0645 crosses the hour to reach 0820 hours.

questions.stem: A roster allots 7.5 hours to patrol and 1.25 hours to briefing. Total hours?
questions.why: Seven and a half hours plus one and a quarter is eight and three quarters.

questions.stem: A grant covers three eighths of a $24,000 training budget. Amount covered?
questions.why: One eighth of twenty-four thousand is three thousand, so three eighths is nine thousand.

questions.stem: A suspect covers 100 meters in 20 seconds. Speed in meters per second?
questions.why: One hundred meters divided by twenty seconds gives five meters each second.

questions.stem: A 240-page case file is 15 percent photographs. How many photo pages?
questions.why: Fifteen percent of two hundred forty is thirty-six photo pages in total.

questions.stem: Three shifts log 18, 24 and 21 citations. Average citations per shift?
questions.why: The three shifts total sixty-three citations, which divides evenly into twenty-one per shift.

questions.stem: A memo states the review 'will proceed absent objection.' The review proceeds if:
questions.why: Absent objection means nothing is filed to stop the review from moving forward.

questions.stem: An order tells officers to act 'at their discretion.' The order:
options: leaves the choice to the officer
questions.why: Discretion hands the decision to the officer rather than dictating one fixed method.

questions.stem: A report says the witness 'declined to elaborate.' The witness:
questions.why: Declining to elaborate means the witness stopped short of adding more detail.

questions.stem: A log entry marked 'inconclusive' describes a finding that is:
questions.why: Inconclusive means the evidence did not settle the question either way.

questions.stem: A supervisor notes the unit is 'running lean.' The staffing is:
questions.why: Running lean means the unit is working with fewer people than planned.

questions.stem: A finding described as 'provisional' is one that is:
questions.why: Provisional findings hold for now and can change as review continues.

questions.stem: Choose the sentence with correct subject and verb agreement.
options: Each of the officers carries a radio.
Each of the officers carry a radio.
Each of the officer carry a radio.
Each of the officer carries a radio.
questions.why: Each is singular, so the verb takes the singular form carries.

questions.stem: Choose the sentence with the correct pronoun case.
options: Between you and I the report is done.
Between you and me the report is done.
Between me and I the report is done.
Between we and you the report is done.
questions.why: A preposition takes object pronouns, so between you and me is correct.

questions.stem: Choose the sentence with correct punctuation between clauses.
options: The officer checked the gate then she left.
The officer checked the gate, then she left.
The officer checked the gate; then she left.
The officer checked the gate then, she left.
questions.why: Two independent clauses need a semicolon or a comma plus conjunction.

questions.stem: Choose the sentence that uses the correct past perfect verb form.
options: The officer had wrote the report before leaving.
The officer has wrote the report before leaving.
The officer have written the report before leaving.
The officer had written the report before leaving.
questions.why: Past perfect pairs had with the participle written, not the simple past wrote.

questions.stem: Choose the sentence written in active voice.
options: The officer secured the evidence bag.
The evidence bag was secured by officers.
Securing of the evidence was done.
The bag was secured by the officer.
questions.why: Active voice puts the officer first as the one doing the action.

questions.stem: No one without a badge enters the yard. Hale entered the yard. Therefore Hale:
questions.why: Since badge-less people never enter, Hale must have carried a valid badge.

questions.stem: If the gate is locked, the lot is empty. The lot is not empty. Therefore:
questions.why: A locked gate would empty the lot, so the open lot proves the gate was unlocked.

questions.stem: Every certified officer completed the course. Reyes is not certified. Therefore Reyes:
questions.why: The course requirement covered certified officers only, so Reyes falls outside that group.

questions.stem: Stops are ordered: P before Q, R after Q, S before P. Which stop comes last?
questions.why: The chain runs S then P then Q then R, placing R last.

questions.stem: Monthly stops were 48, 60, 54 and 42. What is the median?
questions.why: Sorted as 42, 48, 54 and 60, the middle pair averages fifty-one.

questions.stem: A table shows 24 force reports one year and 18 the next. Percent change?
questions.why: A drop of six from a base of twenty-four equals twenty-five percent.

questions.stem: A monthly chart lists 12, 15, 15, 18 and 20 citations. What is the mode?
questions.why: The mode is the value appearing most often, and fifteen appears twice.

questions.stem: The suspect drove a silver sedan with plate 7XK-330. What was the plate?
questions.why: Detail recall: the letters keep their order and the last digits are three three zero.

questions.stem: The burglary occurred between 2100 and 2130 hours. The time window was:
questions.why: Detail recall: both the start and end times were recorded exactly.

questions.stem: The witness described a green pickup with ladder racks. Vehicle color?
questions.why: Detail recall: the color stated in the description was green.

questions.stem: 'The deputy was exonerated by the review.' Exonerated means:
questions.why: To exonerate is to clear someone of blame or wrongdoing.

questions.stem: 'A cursory search of the vehicle' describes a search that was:
questions.why: Cursory means hasty and lacking in depth or detail.

questions.stem: 'The directive was superseded by a later memo.' The directive was:
questions.why: Supersede means to take the place of something earlier.

questions.stem: A driver refuses to exit and reaches under the seat. Your first priority?
options: ask the driver to calm down
write the citation before you approach
order hands visible and request backup
open the door and pull him out
questions.why: Control the hands and add cover before anything else happens.

questions.stem: A colleague arrives visibly impaired before shift. You should:
options: cover his duties and say nothing
send him home and log it later
ignore it since he seems functional
notify the supervisor before shift starts
questions.why: Policy requires reporting impairment before that colleague takes the street.

questions.stem: A resident offers you a $20 gift card for handling her case. You should:
options: decline politely and document the offer
accept it and record it plainly
take it and split it quietly
accept quietly and tell no one
questions.why: Gifts tied to a case are barred, so decline and put the offer on record.
